_how_to_add: Put the image in assets/charts/ (optionally also a smaller .webp for display), then add an entry at the TOP of 'charts' (newest first): file = full-size image, display = optional smaller version shown in the card, title, caption, credit, source (optional URL), added (YYYY-MM-DD). The page sorts by 'added', newest first. Optional: chart_date (YYYY-MM-DD, the chart's own date; tie-break within the same 'added' day, newest first) and tags (e.g. ["Stocks"]; tag filter buttons appear automatically).

charts.title: 10 Year Rate Cycles
charts.caption: Third-party chart, shown as published; it illustrates a cycle theory, not established fact. The US 10-year Treasury yield since the late 1800s against the S&P 500, split into recession, recovery and expansion phases of roughly 180–247 months, with a sine-wave panel marking the 1940 low, the 1981 high and the 2019 low. It projects a pivot cross in 2033 and a recession starting in late 2034.

charts.title: SPX Quartercent Cycles Theory
charts.caption: Third-party chart, shown as published; it illustrates a cycle theory, not established fact. S&P 500 on a log scale from 1927 to the present, overlaid with a sine-wave cycle of roughly 25-year expansion phases separated by about 9–12-year 'Pause' periods (1929–42, 1966–75, 2000–09), with projected markers at '28, '34 and '41.

charts.title: Realized Market Cap RSI | Weekly
charts.caption: Third-party chart, shown as published; an indicator reading, not established fact. Bitcoin with its realized market cap and a weekly RSI panel that marks bull-market ceilings (RSI 100), the 50 'relative position' level (Dec 2014, Oct 2018, May 2022, Mar 2026) and bear-market lows.

charts.title: Gold 10/4 Cycles Theory
charts.caption: Third-party chart, shown as published; it illustrates a cycle theory, not established fact. Gold on a log scale since 1968, alternating roughly 10–11-year bull phases with 4–5-year bear phases, with top and bottom events and a sine-wave 'trigger zone' panel. It projects a bear phase from 2026 to 2030/31.

charts.title: Cycle Runs and Drawdowns
charts.caption: Third-party chart, shown as published; it illustrates a cycle theory, not established fact. Bitcoin on a log scale with bull runs of roughly 1,056 days (+700,000%, +11,800%, +2,100%, +732%) and drawdowns (−86%, −84%, −77%, and −52% as of April 2026), with a halving-cycle sine wave.
